prompt: Who is a defect report written for, by this lesson?
hint: Think about who was in the room when it failed.

choices.text: For the tester who found it, as a note to come back to
choices.why: A private note can lean on memory; a report cannot, because its reader has none of yours.

choices.text: For somebody who was not there when it failed
choices.why: Right: everything they need has to be on the page, because asking you is what the report saves.

choices.text: For the manager, who counts reports to judge the release
choices.why: Counting reports is lesson 16's theatre; the reader who matters is the one who must see the failure again.

choices.text: For the developer who wrote the code, so only they need to follow it
choices.why: Others read it too: triage, the retester, whoever finds a duplicate. And the developer was not there either.

prompt: Which title does the most work in a list of forty reports?
hint: A title is searched and compared with its neighbours.

choices.text: Error on the booking page
choices.why: It matches every defect that page will ever have, so nobody can tell this one from the rest.

choices.text: URGENT: booking is completely broken again, please fix it today!!
choices.why: Urgency is priority's field, "completely" is false, and "again" accuses without a fact.

choices.text: Quantity that is not a whole number answers 500 with a traceback
choices.why: Right: what fails, where and under what condition, in words somebody would search for.

choices.text: Wrap the int() call in book() with a try/except so it stops failing
choices.why: That is a guess at the fix, in the developer's territory, and a customer-facing reader cannot search for it.

prompt: Why does the expected result of Ana's report cite R4 and R7?
hint: Without it, whose word is it?

choices.text: The requirement then argues the case, not Ana's opinion
choices.why: Right: the developer can disagree with you, but has to argue with the requirement.

choices.text: Trackers refuse to save a report with no requirement id in it
choices.why: No tracker in this course does; the reason is the argument, not a form.

choices.text: So that the severity can be read straight off the requirement
choices.why: Severity is judged from the harm; the same requirement can fail trivially or critically.

choices.text: It tells the developer which line of code to change
choices.why: A requirement says what should happen, never where in the code; the traceback points at the line.

prompt: A report is the sentence "I did this, I should have seen that, and I saw something else". Put its fields in that order.
hint: Start before the first action.
trap: Putting the actual result before the steps asks the reader to judge a failure they have not seen how to reach.

prompt: While reproducing the traceback, Ana also sees "cannot be useed" on an order page. What does she file?
hint: Think about the day one of them is fixed.

choices.text: One report covering both, since she found them in the same session
choices.why: When one is fixed the report closes, and the other is forgotten with it.

choices.text: Only the traceback, because a typo is not worth a report
choices.why: Trivial severity is still a defect; the triage decides whether it waits, not the tester by silence.

choices.text: One report with the typo as a comment on the traceback
choices.why: A comment is invisible to search and to the board; the typo would never get its own fix or retest.

choices.text: Two reports, one per defect
choices.why: Right: different lines, different fixes, perhaps different days. One report per defect.

prompt: Why does a reproduction start by asking /health for the version?
hint: What happens if the developer runs another one?

choices.text: To check that the server is fast enough to test
choices.why: /health says whether it is up and which version; it says nothing about speed.

choices.text: So the reader runs the version you ran
choices.why: Right: on another version the defect may be gone, and the report comes back as cannot reproduce.

choices.text: Because a request fails until /health has been called once
choices.why: Nothing in boxoffice depends on /health being called first.

choices.text: To reset the application to its seeded state before the steps
choices.why: /health only reads; resetting is stopping and starting the program.

prompt: Without the e-mail field, the request gets "Sign up before you book." What does that tell Ana about the reproduction?
hint: Did the failure still happen?

choices.text: That the defect is in the sign-up code, not in booking
choices.why: The sign-up check simply runs first and answers before the quantity is read.

choices.text: That the e-mail is a second defect to report
choices.why: Refusing a booking with no account is what R4 asks for.

choices.text: That the field is needed: without it the failure is never reached
choices.why: Right: a field earns its place when taking it away makes the failure disappear.

choices.text: That the reproduction is intermittent
choices.why: It changed because the request changed; the same request gives the same answer every time.

prompt: An empty quantity and 2.5 both answer 500; 7 gets "You can book 1 to 6 tickets." What should the title say?
hint: Name the class, not the example.

choices.text: Typing "two" in the tickets box answers 500
choices.why: True, and a developer who fixes only the word is caught by the next empty box.

choices.text: A quantity that is not a whole number answers 500
choices.why: Right: the neighbours showed the shape, and the shape is what gets fixed.

choices.text: Any quantity outside 1 to 6 answers 500
choices.why: 7 is outside and gets the right sentence; the capture rules this out.

choices.text: The booking form fails with some values, sometimes
choices.why: It fails every time, for a class of values the report can name.

prompt: In the reproduction, `-o /dev/null` throws the page away and `-w '%{http_code}\n'` prints only the ___ code.
hint: Three digits: 500 here.

prompt: A defect appears on some tries and not others. Which line belongs in the report?
hint: What does the reader need to believe a clean try?

choices.text: Happens sometimes, so try a few times
choices.why: A reader whose single try is clean cannot tell whether the defect is gone.

choices.text: Cannot reproduce reliably, closing until it happens again
choices.why: Closing is the triage's decision, and a count would have kept it open.

choices.text: 3 of 10 attempts, same steps, same build
choices.why: Right: a count tells the reader how many tries to make before believing their result.

choices.text: Random failure, probably the network
choices.why: A guess at the cause, with nothing the reader can check.

prompt: What is the difference between severity and priority?
hint: One is measured, one is decided.

choices.text: None: priority is severity rounded to three steps
choices.why: They usually agree, and the cases where they do not are why both exist.

choices.text: Severity is the harm; priority is how soon it gets fixed
choices.why: Right: the tester measures the first from the product; the triage decides the second.

choices.text: Severity is for customers and priority for developers
choices.why: Both are read by everybody at triage; they answer different questions.

choices.text: Severity is set by the product owner and priority by the tester
choices.why: The other way round, normally: the tester proposes severity, the owner decides priority.

prompt: Match each boxoffice 1.1 defect to the severity this lesson's scale gives it.
hint: Money for everybody, a workaround, a scroll, a word.

pairs.left: Students are charged R$ 144,00 for two Hamlet tickets
A word in the tickets box answers 500 with a traceback
The shows table is 760 pixels wide on a phone
"An order that is used cannot be useed."

prompt: R5 says students pay half. Two Hamlet tickets cost R$ 80,00 each. What should a student booking two pay in all, in reais?
hint: 1.1 charged R$ 144,00.

prompt: Why is the 760-pixel shows table minor and still P1?
hint: Did the defect change, or did something around it?

choices.text: The tester raised its severity so it would be fixed sooner
choices.why: It stayed minor; raising severity for attention is what the lesson warns against.

choices.text: Most tickets sell on phones and the campaign starts next week
choices.why: Right: the harm per customer is small, and the cost of leaving it just went up.

choices.text: Layout defects are always fixed first because they are easy
choices.why: Easy fixes do not jump the queue by themselves; this one moved for a business reason.

choices.text: R8 is a more important requirement than R5
choices.why: Requirements are not ranked; the student price is critical and P1 too.

prompt: Lesson 14 found the tickets field has a placeholder and no label. For a screen-reader user it is unclear what the box is for. Which severity fits by this lesson's scale?
hint: Ask who meets it and whether there is a way round.

choices.text: Trivial, because it is only an attribute in the HTML
choices.why: Severity is the harm, not the size of the change; a one-attribute fix can mend a major defect.

choices.text: Minor, because sighted customers book normally
choices.why: For the customers who meet it, it is worse than inconvenient: without a label they do not know what to type.

choices.text: Major: R9 fails for some users, who are left stuck
choices.why: Right: R9 fails for a group of customers; the rest are unaffected, which keeps it below critical.

choices.text: Critical, because accessibility defects are critical by law
choices.why: The scale asks about the harm and who meets it; there is no category that is critical by definition.

prompt: Why is the traceback pasted as text rather than as a screenshot of the same lines?
hint: What can a reader do with text?

choices.text: Text is searchable, copyable and comparable character by character
choices.why: Right: and it reads on a phone, which a screenshot of a terminal does not.

choices.text: Screenshots are not accepted by most trackers
choices.why: Every tracker in lesson 17 takes attachments; the reason is what the reader can do with it.

choices.text: A screenshot would show the password
choices.why: This page shows no password; the reason holds for any traceback.

choices.text: Text proves the defect is reproducible
choices.why: Reproducibility comes from the steps and the count; text is just the best form of evidence.

prompt: What does the server's line `"POST /book HTTP/1.1" 500 -` add that the curl transcript does not?
hint: Who wrote each one?

choices.text: The cause of the failure, which the transcript leaves out
choices.why: The log line holds no cause; the traceback in the transcript is what names a line of code.

choices.text: The server's own record of the request, tied to a moment
choices.why: Right: what the server thought it did, and when, so a developer can find it in a shared log.

choices.text: Proof that the request came from outside the machine
choices.why: 127.0.0.1 says the opposite: the request came from this machine.

choices.text: The version of boxoffice that answered
choices.why: The line has no version; /health and the footer give it.

prompt: Ana is attaching evidence to a report in the company tracker. Which of these should she remove or blur first? Choose all that apply.
hint: Look at it as a stranger would.

choices.text: A real customer's e-mail in a screenshot
choices.why: Yes: another person's data in a tracker many people read is a leak.

choices.text: A session token visible in the address bar
choices.why: Yes: a token lets whoever reads it act as that account.

choices.text: The last line of the traceback
choices.why: That line is the evidence; it names the failure and the value.

choices.text: The address bar showing /book
choices.why: It tells the reader which page it was; a good screenshot keeps it.

prompt: The traceback shows file paths and code to whoever triggers it. Ana's company tracker is open to every employee and to two outside agencies. What does she do?
hint: Exact for the fixers, not for everybody.

choices.text: Leave the reproduction out, so nobody can trigger it
choices.why: The people fixing it need the reproduction as much as anybody.

choices.text: File it as usual, since it is only a test build and nothing can leak from it
choices.why: The same code ships to production; the report describes how to make the real page leak.

choices.text: Use the security route: restricted readers, exact reproduction
choices.why: Right: who sees it is restricted; how exact it is, is not.

choices.text: Tell the developer in a chat message and file nothing in the tracker
choices.why: A chat message is not tracked, not retested and not found again.

prompt: Rui marks Ana's report "cannot reproduce": his copy answers the right sentence for "two". What should Ana check first?
hint: The first line of a reproduction.

choices.text: Whether Rui typed the word in capitals
choices.why: Possible, but the version explains a clean result before any detail of typing does.

choices.text: Which version each of them is running
choices.why: Right: if Rui runs a build where it is fixed, both are right, and the report should say which version it was.

choices.text: Whether her severity was too high for a developer to bother
choices.why: Severity does not make a defect appear or disappear on another machine.

choices.text: Whether Rui used curl instead of the browser
choices.why: Curl and the browser send the same request and get the same answer.

prompt: Order the moves that turn Ana's afternoon into a reproduction a stranger can replay.
hint: State first, the shape last.
items: Restart boxoffice and confirm the version with /health
Send the failing request as one curl command
Remove each field and keep the ones the failure needs
Try neighbouring values to find the class that fails
trap: Trying neighbours before cutting the steps tests variations of a path that still carries noise.

prompt: A report reads: title "Refund accepted for a used order"; steps 1 to 5; expected "refused, as R6 allows refunds only of paid orders"; actual "Order is now refunded." What is missing that a developer needs first?
hint: Which field would make him ask "on what?"

choices.text: A priority, so he knows how soon to fix it
choices.why: The triage sets priority; the developer cannot even reproduce it yet.

choices.text: A guess at which line of code is wrong
choices.why: A good report leaves the cause to the person who owns the code.

choices.text: A screenshot of the order page
choices.why: The actual result is already quoted as text, which is better evidence.

choices.text: The environment: which version, and from what state
choices.why: Right: without it he does not know what to run or where to start.
